Split the output of a command into lines

Source: R/parse_output.R
parse_output.Rd

Splits an output stream of a run(), run_bin() or run_pipeline() result into lines.

Usage

parse_output(
  res,
  stream = c("stdout", "stderr", "both", "plain"),
  trim = FALSE
)

Arguments

res

A run(), run_bin() or run_pipeline() result, another list with stdout or stderr elements, or a character vector for stream = "plain". For a pipeline result, "stdout" is the output of the last command, the only one whose standard output is captured. "stderr" joins the captured standard error of every command, in command order. parse_output() cannot split a raw stream, from binary = TRUE, into lines. Use the raw vector itself, for example with writeBin().

stream

Character string selecting the output source: "stdout" (the default), "stderr", "both" or "plain".

  • "stdout" and "stderr" abort when that stream was not captured (redirected to a file or discarded, NA in the result).

  • "both" gives all of the standard output, then all of the standard error. The order in which the command wrote to the two streams is lost. parse_output() leaves out a stream that was not captured. It aborts only if neither stream was captured.

  • "plain" reads res itself, a character vector without missing values. parse_output() joins its elements with line ends.

Other values abort with class condathis_invalid_stream.

trim

Logical. Whether to remove whitespace at the start and end of each line, and blank lines at the start and end of the output. Defaults to FALSE. Values other than TRUE and FALSE abort with class condathis_invalid_trim.

Value

A character vector with one line per element, without line ends. character(0) for empty output. A res that cannot be read aborts with class condathis_parse_output_invalid_res (also condathis_invalid_res), and a raw stream with condathis_parse_output_binary_stream.

Details

Lines end at a line feed, a carriage return and line feed pair, or a carriage return alone, so the result is the same on every operating system. parse_output() removes the line ends, and a line end at the end of the output does not start one more, empty line. It keeps the rest of the text as the command wrote it: spaces and tabs at the start and end of lines, and blank lines. Empty output gives character(0).

trim = TRUE also removes whitespace at the start and end of each line, and blank lines at the start and end of the output. This is useful for a single value, such as a version string. It changes tab-separated output with empty first or last fields, and indented text such as YAML.

See also

Other commands: run(), run_bin(), run_pipeline(), run_step()

Examples

# A list with the output fields of a `run()` result
res <- list(
  stdout = "line1\nline2\nline3\n",
  stderr = "error1\nerror2\n"
)

# Parse the standard output
parse_output(res, stream = "stdout")
#> [1] "line1" "line2" "line3"

# Parse the standard error
parse_output(res, stream = "stderr")
#> [1] "error1" "error2"

# Merge both
parse_output(res, stream = "both")
#> [1] "line1"  "line2"  "line3"  "error1" "error2"

# Parse plain text
plain_text <- "This is line one.\nThis is line two.\nThis is line three."
parse_output(plain_text, stream = "plain")
#> [1] "This is line one."   "This is line two."   "This is line three."

# Whitespace is kept: the empty first field of this tab-separated line
# stays in place
parse_output("\tchr1\t100\n", stream = "plain")
#> [1] "\tchr1\t100"

# Remove it when only the text matters
parse_output("  2.9.0  \n\n", stream = "plain", trim = TRUE)
#> [1] "2.9.0"
